drill.titleSentence: Dates and times in a sentence
drills.genderChen: Diminutives ending in -chen and -lein are always neuter.
drills.genderDays: Days, months and seasons are masculine.
drills.genderE: Most nouns ending in -e are feminine (about nine in ten).
drills.genderGe: Many nouns starting with Ge- are neuter (das Gebäude, das Gemüse).
drills.genderIn: Female forms ending in -in are feminine (die Lehrerin).
drills.genderLing: Nouns ending in -ling, -ismus, -or, -ist and -ant are masculine.
drills.genderMent: Nouns ending in -ment, -um and -ma are usually neuter.
drills.hintArticleDefault: Learn every noun together with its article: the article is part of the word.
drills.hintAuxSein: {verb} takes "sein": movement from A to B or a change of state.
drills.hintAuxVaries: {verb} takes "sein" for movement (ist gefahren) and "haben" with an object (hat das Auto gefahren).
drills.hintClock: Formal: hour + "Uhr" + minutes (24-hour clock). Everyday: "nach", "vor", "halb" (half TO the next hour), "Viertel".
drills.hintCompound: A compound takes the gender of its last part: {last} → {whole}.
drills.hintDate: Ordinal + month: "der {ordinal} …" after "Heute ist", "am {ordinal}n …" after "am". Month {month} = {monthDe}.
drills.hintMeaningDefault: Think of a sentence you would use it in.
drills.hintNumber: Units before tens, joined with "und": {pieces}. One word, no spaces.
drills.hintOrdinal: Ordinals 1-19 end in -te (erste, dritte, siebte, achte are irregular), from 20 in -ste; after "am" add -n.
drills.hintPreterite: Irregular verbs change their stem in the Präteritum: {infinitive} → {preterite}.
drills.hintPrice: Euros first, then the cents, usually without "Cent": "drei Euro vierzig".
drills.instrClock: Say the time in German. Formal or everyday both count.
drills.instrDate: Say the date in words, as in "Heute ist …" or "am …".
drills.instrPrice: The cashier reads the price aloud. Write what they say.
drills.instrSentence: Translate. Write the date and the time in words.
drills.numberHundreds: hundreds and thousands come first, all in one word
drills.pluralDie: The plural always takes "die", whatever the gender.
drills.pluralE: Many masculine nouns add -e in the plural.
drills.pluralEUmlaut: This one adds -e and an umlaut, like der Stuhl → die Stühle.
drills.pluralErUmlaut: This one adds -er and an umlaut, like das Haus → die Häuser.
drills.pluralFeminine: Feminine nouns usually add -n or -en in the plural.
drills.pluralS: Words from English and French, and words ending in a vowel, often add -s.
drills.pluralSame: Masculine and neuter nouns ending in -er, -el and -en often stay the same in the plural.

exam.ratingPrompt:
You are an examiner in the speaking part of a German exam at {level} level. Task: {task}. The candidate said: "{said}". Rate the candidate as in the Goethe exams on four criteria from 0 (not at all) to 4 (fully): Erfüllung (was the task done, with its points?), Kohärenz (connected, understandable speech, reacting to the examiner), Wortschatz (range and fitness of the words for {level}), Strukturen (grammar: correctness and variety for {level}). Do not write a corrected text. Answer in exactly this form, with these German labels, and nothing else:
Erfüllung: <0-4>
Kohärenz: <0-4>
Wortschatz: <0-4>
Strukturen: <0-4>
Kommentar: <two sentences in English: what was good, what was missing>
Tipp: <one concrete thing to do better next time, in English>
Besser: <one single sentence the candidate said, corrected and improved, in German>
exam.part.a1-1: Introduce yourself with the seven points: name, age, country, home town, languages, job, hobby. Then spell a word or say a number.
exam.part.a1-2: A topic and two word cards: ask a question with the first, answer the examiner's question with the second.
exam.part.a1-3: Two pictures, described in words: ask politely for each; the examiner reacts.
exam.part.a2-1: Four keyword cards about a person's life: ask the examiner a question with each, and answer the examiner's questions.
exam.part.a2-2: A topic with four guiding points: talk for about a minute, then answer one or two questions.
exam.part.a2-3: Plan something with the examiner as your partner: make suggestions, react, agree.
exam.part.b1-1: Plan something with the examiner as your partner, using the points on the sheet.
exam.part.b1-2: Present a topic in five slides: introduce it, your experience, the situation in your country, advantages and disadvantages with your opinion, a closing. About three minutes.
exam.part.b1-3: The examiner gives feedback on your presentation and asks questions; answer them.
exam.part.b2-1: A talk of about four minutes on a topic with three guiding points; then a question from the examiner.
exam.part.b2-2: A thesis to discuss: take a position, react to the examiner's counter-arguments, defend yours.
exam.part.c1-1: A structured talk of three to four minutes on a social topic with guiding points; then a question.
exam.part.c1-2: A discussion on a thesis: argue, respond to objections, weigh positions.
exam.part.c2-1: A talk of about five minutes on a demanding topic with guiding points; then a question.
exam.part.c2-2: A discussion with the examiner on a thesis, at full argumentative range.

pron.title: Sounds to check
pron.note: The recognizer mishears too; say the sentence once more, a little slower, before you blame your mouth.
pron.ue: ü: say "ee" and round your lips as for "oo" without moving your tongue.
pron.oe: ö: say "eh" and round your lips; the tongue stays forward.
pron.ae: ä is an open "e" as in "bed", never "ah".
pron.ach: ch after a, o, u, au is the rough sound at the back of the throat, like clearing it softly; not "k", not "sh".
pron.ich: ch after e, i, ä, ö, ü, l, n, r and in -chen is the soft hiss of a whispered "y" in "yes".
pron.ig: a final -ig is said like -ich: zwanzig, wichtig.
pron.z: z is "ts" from the first letter: Zeit, zehn, Katze.
pron.w: w is the English "v": Wasser, wir.
pron.v: v is usually "f": vier, Vater, viel.
pron.ei: ei rhymes with "eye": eins, mein, Zeit.
pron.ie: ie is a long "ee": vier, sie, Liebe.
pron.eu: eu and äu sound like "oy": neun, heute, Häuser.
pron.stsp: st and sp at the start of a word or syllable are "sht" and "shp": Straße, sprechen.
pron.s: an s before a vowel is voiced, like the "z" in "zoo": sieben, Sonne.
pron.final: a final b, d, g is said as p, t, k: Tag, Kind, halb.
pron.h: an h after a vowel is silent and makes the vowel long: Bahn, sehr, Uhr.
pron.r: r sits at the back of the throat like a soft gargle; at the end of a word it fades to a short "a": Mutter, hier.
pron.sz: ß is a sharp, voiceless "s" after a long vowel: Straße, heißen.
pron.pf: pf: say both sounds, a quick p into f: Pferd, Kopf.
pron.j: j is the English "y": ja, Jahr.
pron.ng: ng as in "sing", with no hard g after it: lang, Zeitung.
pron.long: a long word: say it part by part, with the stress on the first part, then join the parts.

Bonus squares work only under new tiles; all seven tiles in one go earn {bonus} extra. The game ends when the bag is empty and one rack runs out, or after four scoreless turns in a row.

together.wordleIntro: {a} and {b} take turns guessing the same five-letter German word on one board. Whoever hits it wins the word.
together.wordleNotAWord: Not a word the lexicon knows
together.wordleRules: Green: right letter, right place. Amber: in the word, but elsewhere. Grey: not in the word. Every guess must be a real German word, and {tries} guesses are all you get for a word. A match is {n} words; the player who finds more wins.
together.wordleRulesHints: Stuck? After {hint} guesses the board gives away the article, after {last} the meaning, and from then on the word can be revealed and skipped.
together.whoamiDetail: Keep a secret card; the other asks yes/no questions in German and guesses.
together.whoamiRules: One of you sees a secret card: a person, an animal, a thing or a place. The other asks questions in German that can be answered with ja or nein - {total} at most - and then guesses. Whoever keeps the secret answers only ja, nein or jein, and reads out a hint when asked; each hint costs a point. A right guess earns the questions left over, plus five. Then swap.
together.whoamiPass: Pass the phone to {name}; {other} must not look yet.
together.whoamiAnswerHint: Answer only with ja, nein or jein, and tap what you said.
together.whoamiLastGuess: No questions left - one last guess, {name}.
together.whoamiReadOut: Read the hints out loud; don’t show the screen.
